title: Cohomology of groups
summary: Homology and cohomology of arbitrary groups with coefficients in k-linear representations on Mathlib's carriers: conjugation and quotient actions, hyper(co)homology, permutation complexes and trees, cup and cap products, Künneth and universal coefficients, the Pontryagin ring, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence with edge maps, transgression, products and Hopf's formula, the double coset formula, and for finite groups stable elements, Tate duality and periodicity.

layers.title: Conjugation, quotient actions and permutation modules

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.conj
targets.statement: For H ≤ G and g ∈ G, conjugation c_g : Hⁿ(H, M) → Hⁿ(gHg⁻¹, M) is the compatible-pair map of (x ↦ g⁻¹xg, m ↦ g·m); likewise c_g : Hₙ(H, M) → Hₙ(gHg⁻¹, M) from (h ↦ ghg⁻¹, m ↦ g·m), and on Ĥⁿ(H, M) for finite G. Conjugation by an element of H is the identity on the (co)homology of H.

locator.where: Ch. I §2, corollary to Prop. 2, p. 113 (HS53 line 154–160)

api.name: conj_one
api.statement: c_1 is the identity.

api.name: conj_mul
api.statement: c_{gh} = c_g ∘ c_h after g(hHh⁻¹)g⁻¹ = (gh)H(gh)⁻¹.

api.name: conj_eq_id_of_mem
api.statement: For g ∈ H, c_g is the identity of Hⁿ(H, M), Hₙ(H, M) and Ĥⁿ(H, M).

api.name: conj_naturality
api.statement: c_g commutes with coefficient maps, connecting maps, restriction to K ≤ H, corestriction and transfer for finite-index K ≤ H, and homological corestriction.

api.name: conj_zero
api.statement: In degree 0, c_g(m) = g·m on M^H and c_g[m] = [g·m] on M_H.

tests.name: conj_S3_transposition
tests.statement: G = S₃, H = ⟨(12)⟩, g = (13), 𝔽₂: c_g sends the nonzero character of H to the character of ⟨(23)⟩ with value 1.

tests.name: conj_wrong_direction
tests.statement: For g = (123), gHg⁻¹ = ⟨(23)⟩ but g⁻¹Hg = ⟨(13)⟩: conjugating by g⁻¹ lands in the wrong subgroup.

tests.name: conj_abelian_trivial
tests.statement: For abelian G and trivial coefficients, c_g is the identity.

tests.name: conj_outer_nontrivial
tests.statement: G = S₃, H = A₃, g = (12), 𝔽₃: c_g acts by −1 on H¹(A₃, 𝔽₃) ≅ 𝔽₃, so inner triviality needs g ∈ H.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.quotientRep
targets.statement: For N ◁ G and Q = G ⧸ N, the representations of Q on Hⁿ(N, M) and Hₙ(N, M) given by qN ↦ c_q; in degree 0 they are M^N (Rep.quotientToInvariantsFunctor) and M_N (Rep.quotientToCoinvariantsFunctor).

locator.where: Ch. I §7, description of the G/K-operators, p. 117–118 (HS53 line 345–354)

api.name: quotientRep_functorial
api.statement: Functorial in M; connecting maps of short exact sequences of G-representations are Q-equivariant.

api.name: quotientRep_naturality
api.statement: Natural for morphisms of pairs (G', N') → (G, N) with f(N') ≤ N.

api.name: quotientRep_zero
api.statement: In degree 0 the representation is Rep.quotientToInvariantsFunctor N M, respectively the coinvariant one.

api.name: quotientRep_H1_trivial
api.statement: If N acts trivially on M, H¹(N, M) ≅ Hom(N^ab, M) with (gN·φ)(n) = g·φ(g⁻¹ng).

tests.name: quotientRep_extremes
tests.statement: N = G gives the trivial group Q; N = 1 gives M in degree 0 and zero above.

tests.name: quotientRep_S3
tests.statement: G = S₃, N = A₃, 𝔽₃: the transposition acts by −1 on H¹(A₃, 𝔽₃), so the invariants vanish.

tests.name: quotientRep_coefficient_action
tests.statement: G = ℤ/4, N = 2ℤ/4, M = ℤ with generator acting by −1: on H⁰(N, M) = M the action is −1; the model ignoring the coefficient action gives +1.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.sigmaIso
targets.statement: For a family (M_i)_{i : ι}, ⊕ᵢ Hₙ(G, M_i) → Hₙ(G, ⊕ᵢ M_i) and Hⁿ(G, ∏ᵢ M_i) → ∏ᵢ Hⁿ(G, M_i) are isomorphisms; for finite ι cohomology commutes with direct sums.

locator.where: Ch. III (homology commutes with direct sums; uncertified)

tests.name: sigma_point
tests.statement: For ι a point both maps are identities.

tests.name: pi_not_sum
tests.statement: A = ℤ^(ℕ) trivial action: the identity of A lies in H¹(A, ℤ^(ℕ)) = Hom(A, ℤ^(ℕ)) but not in ⊕ Hom(A, ℤ).

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.permutationIso
targets.statement: Natural isomorphisms Hₙ(G, k[G ⧸ H] ⊗ M) ≅ Hₙ(H, M), Hⁿ(G, Hom_k(k[G ⧸ H], M)) ≅ Hⁿ(H, M), their twisted forms for Ind_H^G k_χ, and for a G-set X with orbit representatives Σ: Hₙ(G, k[X] ⊗ M) ≅ ⊕_{x∈Σ} Hₙ(G_x, M), Hⁿ(G, Hom_k(k[X], M)) ≅ ∏_{x∈Σ} Hⁿ(G_x, M).
hypotheses: X a G-set in Type u

locator.where: II §2.8, p. 168 (Shapiro's lemma for permutation modules)

tests.name: perm_point
tests.statement: X a point: the identity.

tests.name: perm_free
tests.statement: X = G: Hₙ(G, k[G] ⊗ M) = 0 for n > 0.

tests.name: perm_orbits_not_points
tests.statement: G = ℤ/2, X = G ⊔ pt: H₀(G, ℤ[X]) = ℤ², while summing over points gives ℤ³.

targets.name: TauCeti.ContCohomology.discreteIso
targets.statement: For G with the discrete topology, k discrete and A : TopRep k G with discrete carrier, an isomorphism Θₙ : continuousCohomology n A ≅ Hⁿ(G, A) of k-modules, natural in compatible pairs and in A, compatible with connecting maps, agreeing in degrees 0, 1, 2 with ProfiniteCohomology §§3.1–3.2.
hypotheses: A : TopRep k G with discrete carrier

locator.where: Ch. I §2, homogeneous and non-homogeneous cochains, pp. 112–113 (HS53 line 129–141)

api.name: discreteIso_zero
api.statement: Θ₀ identifies both sides with A^G.

api.name: discreteIso_naturality
api.statement: Natural for homomorphisms of discrete groups with compatible maps, and in A.

api.name: discreteIso_finite
api.statement: For k = ℤ and finite G : Type, Θₙ realises TauCeti.ContCohomology.nonempty_continuousCohomology_addEquiv_groupCohomology.

tests.name: discreteIso_trivial
tests.statement: Trivial group: both sides A in degree 0, zero above.

tests.name: discreteIso_Z
tests.statement: G = ℤ discrete, A = ℤ: both sides of Θ₁ are Hom(ℤ, ℤ); with the profinite topology on ℤ, H¹_cont = 0.

tests.name: discreteIso_sign
tests.statement: The homogeneous cocycle f(g₀) − f(g₁) instead of f(g₁) − f(g₀) gives −f, different for G = ℤ, A = ℤ/3.

targets.name: TauCeti.hyperHomology
targets.statement: For C : ChainComplex (Rep k G) ℕ, Hₙ(G; C) is the homology of the total complex of the bicomplex of inhomogeneous chains of the C_q; for D : CochainComplex (Rep k G) ℕ, Hⁿ(G; D) is the cohomology of the total complex of inhomogeneous cochains with values in the D^q. A complex bounded below by b is reindexed to C′_r = C_{r+b}. For k = ℤ and chain complexes this is SchemeKTheoryOperations §6.7's group hyperhomology; the target adds arbitrary k and hypercohomology.

locator.where: Ch. I §4, p. 114, and Ch. I §2 Prop. 1, p. 111

api.name: hyperHomology_map
api.statement: Functorial in chain maps and in compatible pairs (f : G' →* G, C' ⟶ Res_f C).

api.name: hyperHomologyIso
api.statement: For a projective resolution P of k, Hₙ(G; C) ≅ Hₙ(Tot (P_p ⊗ C_q)_G), compatibly for two resolutions; dually for hypercohomology.

api.name: hyperHomology_quasiIso
api.statement: Quasi-isomorphisms induce isomorphisms.

api.name: hyperHomology_single
api.statement: For C concentrated in degree 0 on M, Hₙ(G; C) ≅ Hₙ(G, M); dually Hⁿ(G; D) ≅ Hⁿ(G, M).

api.name: hyperCohomologyIsoDerived
api.statement: Hⁿ(G; D) ≅ Hom in DerivedCategory (Rep k G) from k to D[n], recovering groupCohomologyIsoExt in degree 0.

api.name: hyperHomology_int_comparison
api.statement: For k = ℤ and C in degrees ≥ 0, Hₙ(G; C) is naturally isomorphic to SchemeKTheoryOperations §6.7's group hyperhomology; for integral bounded-below C the reindexing is K3BlochGroups §4.1's.

tests.name: hyper_Z2
tests.statement: G = ℤ/2, C = ℤ in degree 0: H₁ = ℤ/2.

tests.name: hyper_S3
tests.statement: G = S₃, C = ℤ[S₃ ⧸ A₃] → ℤ: H₀ = 0, H₁ = ℤ/2 although the coinvariant complex is acyclic.

tests.name: hyper_trivial_group
tests.statement: For the trivial group Hₙ(1; C) = Hₙ(C).

targets.name: TauCeti.hyperHomology.δ
targets.statement: A degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of representations gives natural long exact sequences in hyperhomology and hypercohomology.
hypotheses: 0 → C' → C → C'' → 0 degreewise short exact

tests.name: les_single
tests.statement: For complexes in degree 0 these are Mathlib's long exact sequences.

tests.name: les_acyclic
tests.statement: If C is acyclic the connecting maps are isomorphisms Hₙ(G; C'') ≅ Hₙ₋₁(G; C').

tests.name: les_trivial_group
tests.statement: For G trivial, the homology sequence of complexes.

targets.name: TauCeti.hyperHomology.spectralSequences
targets.statement: Natural convergent spectral sequences E¹_{p,q} = H_q(G, C_p) ⇒ H_{p+q}(G; C) with d¹ = H_q(G, ∂), E²_{p,q} = H_p(G, H_q(C)) ⇒ H_{p+q}(G; C), and their cohomological duals; if Hᵢ(C) = 0 for i ≤ t then Hₙ(G; C) = 0 for n ≤ t; if the C_p are acyclic, Hₙ(G; C) ≅ Hₙ(C_G). For k = ℤ the homological sequences and the vanishing statement are SchemeKTheoryOperations §6.7's.

locator.where: Ch. I §5, Lemma 1, p. 115; Lemma 2 and Prop. 5, p. 116; Ch. I §4 Prop. 4, p. 114

tests.name: ss_single
tests.statement: C in degree 0: one row, Hₙ(G, C₀).

tests.name: ss_S3_first
tests.statement: For ℤ[S₃ ⧸ A₃] → ℤ: d¹ is the corestriction, iso on q = 0 and zero on q = 1; H₁ = ℤ/2, H₂ = ℤ/3.

tests.name: ss_no_converse
tests.statement: With S₃ ⧸ ⟨(12)⟩, H₀ = H₁ = 0 although H₁(C) ≅ ℤ².

layers.title: Complexes of permutation modules and actions on trees

targets.name: TauCeti.equivariantHomology
targets.statement: H^G_n(C; M) = Hₙ(G; C ⊗ M) and H_G^n(C; M) = Hⁿ(G; Hom_k(C, M)). For C a resolution of k: if every C_p is k-flat, C ⊗ M → M is a quasi-isomorphism and H^G_n(C; M) ≅ Hₙ(G, M); if every C_p is k-projective, M → Hom_k(C, M) is a quasi-isomorphism and H_G^n(C; M) ≅ Hⁿ(G, M). Flatness alone does not give the cohomological statement.
hypotheses: homological comparison: C resolves k and every C_p is flat over k
cohomological comparison: C resolves k and every C_p is projective over k

api.name: equivariantHomology_les
api.statement: A short exact sequence 0 → C' → C → C'' → 0 that stays degreewise short exact after − ⊗ M (e.g. split over k in each degree, M k-flat, or every C''_p k-flat) gives a natural long exact sequence in H^G_*(−; M); one that stays degreewise short exact after Hom_k(−, M) (split over k, M k-injective, or every C''_p k-projective) gives one in H_G^*(−; M).

api.name: equivariantHomology_les_coeff
api.statement: A short exact sequence of representations M gives a long exact sequence in H^G_*(C; −) when every C_p is k-flat and in H_G^*(C; −) when every C_p is k-projective.

api.name: equivariantHomology_map
api.statement: H^G_n covariant and H_G^n contravariant in chain maps, both functorial in M and natural for compatible pairs.

api.name: equivariantHomology_acyclic
api.statement: For a resolution C of k, termwise k-flat: H^G_n(C; M) ≅ Hₙ(G, M); termwise k-projective: H_G^n(C; M) ≅ Hⁿ(G, M); natural in M and compatible with the long exact sequences in the coefficients.

tests.name: eq_standard
tests.statement: For the standard resolution the isomorphism is groupHomologyIso.

tests.name: eq_not_resolution
tests.statement: C = ℤ[ℤ/2] in degree 0: H^G_1 = 0 ≠ H₁(ℤ/2, ℤ).

tests.name: eq_flatness
tests.statement: k = ℤ/4, G trivial, M = ℤ/2, C = k ⊕ (ℤ/2 → ℤ/4 → ℤ/2): C → k quasi-iso but H^G_2 = ℤ/2.

tests.name: eq_projectivity
tests.statement: k = ℤ, G trivial, M = ℤ, C = ℤ ⊕ (F →u F →v ℤ[1/2]) with F = ℤ^(ℕ), u(e_i) = e_i − 2e_{i+1}, v(e_i) = 2^{−i}: flat terms, C → ℤ quasi-iso, but (1, 0, 1, 0, …) is not of the form (a_i − 2a_{i+1}) (a₀ would be −1/3 in ℤ₂), so H_G^2(C; ℤ) ≠ 0 = H²(1, ℤ).

tests.name: eq_les_exactness
tests.statement: G trivial, M = ℤ/2, 0 → ℤ →2 ℤ → ℤ/2 → 0 in degree 0: tensoring gives ℤ/2 →0 ℤ/2 →id ℤ/2, and a long exact sequence would need the zero map H^G_0(C'; M) → H^G_0(C; M) to be injective.

targets.name: TauCeti.equivariantHomology.orbitSpectralSequence
targets.statement: For C_p ≅ ⊕_{σ∈Σ_p} Ind_{G_σ}^G k_σ, the first sequence of 2.3 for C ⊗ M is E¹_{p,q} = ⊕_σ H_q(G_σ, k_σ ⊗ M) ⇒ H^G_{p+q}(C; M), dually E₁^{p,q} = ∏_σ H^q(G_σ, Hom_k(k_σ, M)); d¹ is H_q(G, ∂) through the Shapiro isomorphisms. For k = ℤ, trivial characters and transitive permutation modules this is SchemeKTheoryOperations §6.7's first-page identification.
hypotheses: C_p monomial: ⊕_σ Ind_{G_σ}^G k_σ, χ_σ : G_σ →* kˣ

locator.where: Ch. VII (equivariant spectral sequence; uncertified); the bicomplex is HS53 Ch. I §4, p. 114

tests.name: orbit_fixed
tests.statement: All G_σ = G, trivial characters: E¹_{p,q} = H_q(G, M)^(Σ_p).

tests.name: orbit_tree
tests.statement: For a tree the sequence has two columns and gives 3.5.

tests.name: orbit_reflection_vs_rotation
tests.statement: Circle with two vertices: ℤ/2 by reflection has E¹_{0,q} = H_q(ℤ/2, ℤ)² surviving in odd q ≥ 3; by rotation, all stabilisers trivial.

targets.name: TauCeti.equivariantHomology.free
targets.statement: If every C_p is free over k[G], H^G_n(C; M) ≅ Hₙ((C ⊗ M)_G), with E²_{p,q} = H_p(G, H_q(C ⊗ M)) ⇒ H_{p+q}((C ⊗ M)_G); if C resolves k, Hₙ((C ⊗ M)_G) ≅ Hₙ(G, M).

tests.name: free_cover
tests.statement: For the singular chains of a finite regular cover (AlgebraicTopology §5.3) the abutment is the homology of the base.

tests.name: free_cyclic
tests.statement: G = ℤ/m with the periodic resolution: ℤ/m in odd degrees, 0 in positive even degrees.

tests.name: free_needed
tests.statement: C = ℤ in degree 0: H₁(C_G) = 0 while H₁(G; C) = G^ab.

targets.name: TauCeti.GTree.augmentedChains_exact
targets.statement: For a G-tree X with a G-invariant orientation E⁺, 0 → k[E⁺] → k[V] → k → 0 with ∂e = t(e) − o(e) is an exact sequence of permutation representations, split over k.

tests.name: tree_point
tests.statement: One-vertex tree: 0 → 0 → k → k → 0.

tests.name: tree_line
tests.statement: ℤ acting on the line: ∂ = t − 1 on k[ℤ], injective with cokernel k.

tests.name: tree_loop
tests.statement: One vertex with a loop: ∂ = 0, not exact; acyclicity is used.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.treeSequence
targets.statement: Natural long exact sequences … → ⊕_{e∈Σ₁} Hₙ(G_e, M) → ⊕_{v∈Σ₀} Hₙ(G_v, M) → Hₙ(G, M) → ⊕_{e∈Σ₁} Hₙ₋₁(G_e, M) → … and dually with products in cohomology; vertex maps are corestriction/restriction, and for t(e) = a·v, o(e) = b·w the edge map is c_{a⁻¹}∘cor into v minus c_{b⁻¹}∘cor into w.
hypotheses: Σ₀, Σ₁ orbit representatives of vertices and oriented edges

tests.name: tree_Z_line
tests.statement: ℤ on the line: H₁(ℤ, M) = M^ℤ, H₀(ℤ, M) = M_ℤ, Hₙ = 0 for n ≥ 2.

tests.name: tree_fixed_vertex
tests.statement: One-vertex tree: Hₙ(G_{v₀}, M) = Hₙ(G, M).

tests.name: tree_sum_wrong
tests.statement: With a sum instead of a difference the line gives H₀(ℤ, ℤ) = ℤ/2.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.amalgamSequence
targets.statement: Mayer–Vietoris sequences for amalgams A ∗_C B (Monoid.PushoutI), first map x ↦ (−cor x, cor x), and for HNN extensions (HNNExtension H A B φ), first map the difference of the maps induced by A ≤ H and by ι_B ∘ φ with m ↦ t·m; free products Hₙ(A ∗ B, M) ≅ Hₙ(A, M) ⊕ Hₙ(B, M) for n ≥ 2 and every M, with the degree-one exact sequence 0 → H₁(A, M) ⊕ H₁(B, M) → H₁(A ∗ B, M) → M → M_A ⊕ M_B → M_{A∗B} → 0 (direct sum also for n = 1 when the action is trivial); free groups Hₙ(F, M) = Hⁿ(F, M) = 0 for n ≥ 2 and 0 → H₁(F, M) → M^(S) → M → H₀(F, M) → 0.
hypotheses: A B ≤ H, φ : A ≃* B

tests.name: hnn_BS12
tests.statement: BS(1,2): H₁ = ℤ; the sum instead of the difference gives ℤ/3.

tests.name: free_group
tests.statement: FreeGroup S: H₁ = ℤ^(S), Hₙ = 0 for n ≥ 2; ℤ/2 ∗ ℤ/2 has (ℤ/2)² in odd degrees.

tests.name: free_product_twisted
tests.statement: ℤ ∗ ℤ with M = ℤ, both generators acting by −1: H₁ = ker(−2m_a − 2m_b) ≅ ℤ but H₁(ℤ, M) = 0 for each factor; the kernel of M → M_A ⊕ M_B = (ℤ/2)² is 2ℤ ≅ ℤ.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.cup
targets.statement: For μ : M ⊗ N ⟶ P, (φ ∪ ψ)(g₁,…,g_{p+q}) = μ(φ(g₁,…,g_p) ⊗ (g₁⋯g_p)·ψ(g_{p+1},…,g_{p+q})), with d(φ ∪ ψ) = dφ ∪ ψ + (−1)^p φ ∪ dψ, inducing a k-bilinear ∪_μ : Hᵖ(G, M) × H^q(G, N) → H^{p+q}(G, P).
hypotheses: M N P : Rep k G

locator.where: Ch. II Prop. 1.38 and its proof, p. 73

api.name: cup_bilinear
api.statement: Bilinear, and natural in μ: φ ∪_{μ≫f} ψ = f ∘ (φ ∪_μ ψ).

api.name: cup_descends
api.statement: Cocycles to cocycles, coboundary times cocycle a coboundary.

api.name: cup_zero_zero
api.statement: In bidegree (0,0), (m, n) ↦ μ(m ⊗ n).

tests.name: cup_Z2_square
tests.statement: G = ℤ/2, 𝔽₂: x ∪ x is the nonzero class of H².

tests.name: cup_Z2_witness
tests.statement: On ℤ², the product of the two projections pairs to +1 with [e₁|e₂] − [e₂|e₁]; the (−1)^{pq} convention gives −1.

tests.name: cup_no_twist
tests.statement: Without the action on the second factor, for G = ℤ, N = P = ℤ[ℤ], φ = id, ψ(1) = 1, the product has coboundary 2(t − 1) ≠ 0.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.cup_δ
targets.statement: δx'' ∪ y = δ(x'' ∪ y) and x ∪ δy'' = (−1)^p δ(x ∪ y'') for short exact sequences that stay exact after tensoring; the cup product is the unique family natural in M, N, equal to the invariant product in degree (0,0), satisfying both rules for the coinduction sequences.
hypotheses: short exact sequences whose tensor with the other factor is short exact

locator.where: Ch. II Prop. 1.38(c), (d) and uniqueness, p. 73

tests.name: cup_δ_needs_exact
tests.statement: 0 → ℤ → ℤ → ℤ/2 → 0 tensored with ℤ/2 is not exact.

tests.name: cup_δ_degree_zero
tests.statement: In bidegree (0,0) the rule is the definition of δ applied to μ.

tests.name: cup_Loh_convention
tests.statement: (−1)^{pq} x ∪ y satisfies the right rule without sign and the left rule with (−1)^q; it is −∪ on H¹(ℤ²) × H¹(ℤ²).

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.cup_assoc
targets.statement: ∪ is unital, associative for compatible pairings, graded commutative x ∪_μ y = (−1)^{pq} y ∪_{μ'} x (μ' = μ after the braiding), and natural for compatible pairs, in particular restriction, inflation and coefficient maps.

tests.name: cup_trivial_group
tests.statement: G trivial: μ in degree 0.

tests.name: cup_comm_Z2
tests.statement: x ∪ y = −y ∪ x on H*(ℤ², ℤ).

tests.name: cup_comm_cochains
tests.statement: On cochains x ∪ y and −y ∪ x differ at (e₁, e₂).

targets.name: TauCeti.Rep.DiagonalApprox
targets.statement: A diagonal approximation of a projective resolution P of k is a chain map Δ : P ⟶ P ⊗ P lifting k ≅ k ⊗ k; Alexander–Whitney is one on Rep.standardResolution; two are homotopic after comparison; μ ∘ (φ ⊗ ψ) ∘ Δ computes ∪_μ for every (P, Δ).
hypotheses: P a projective resolution of the trivial representation k

api.name: diagonalApprox_exists
api.statement: Every projective resolution has one, unique up to homotopy.

api.name: cup_eq_diagonalApprox
api.statement: The cup computed with (P, Δ) equals 4.1 through groupCohomologyIso.

tests.name: diag_trivial
tests.statement: G trivial, P = k: Δ is the unitor.

tests.name: diag_Z2
tests.statement: G = ℤ/2: AW and a diagonal of the periodic resolution both give x² ≠ 0.

tests.name: diag_wrong_degree
tests.statement: (g₀..gₙ) ↦ (g₀..gₙ) ⊗ (g₀..gₙ) raises degree to 2n.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.corestriction_cup
targets.statement: For H ≤ G of finite index, x ∈ Hᵖ(H, M), y ∈ H^q(G, N): cor(x ∪ res y) = cor(x) ∪ y and cor(res y ∪ x) = y ∪ cor(x).

tests.name: proj_H_eq_G
tests.statement: H = G: both sides x ∪ y.

tests.name: proj_res
tests.statement: x = res z: [G : H](z ∪ y), consistent with map_subtype_id_comp_corestriction.

tests.name: proj_tate
tests.statement: For finite G agrees with TauCeti.TateCohomology.cup_projection through 4.7(a).

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.cap
targets.statement: Cap product ∩ : Hᵖ(G, M) ⊗ Hₙ(G, N) → Hₙ₋ₚ(G, P) for μ : M ⊗ N ⟶ P through a diagonal approximation, and the evaluation ⟨−,−⟩ : Hⁿ(G, Hom_k(M, A)) ⊗ Hₙ(G, M) → A for trivial A, given on inhomogeneous representatives by ⟨φ, Σ a_i [g_{i,1}|…|g_{i,n}] ⊗ m_i⟩ = Σ a_i φ(g_{i,1}, …, g_{i,n})(m_i), with ⟨dφ, c⟩ = ⟨φ, ∂c⟩ without sign.
hypotheses: A a k-module with trivial action

api.name: cap_projection
api.statement: f_*(f^*x ∩ z) = x ∩ f_*z for f : G' →* G.

api.name: cap_transfer
api.statement: tr(y ∩ z) = res y ∩ tr z and cor(x ∩ tr z) = cor(x) ∩ z, the first cor homological Hₙ₋ₚ(H, P) → Hₙ₋ₚ(G, P), the second cohomological Hᵖ(H, M) → Hᵖ(G, M).

api.name: eval_cup
api.statement: ⟨x ∪ y, z⟩ = ⟨x, y ∩ z⟩ for x ∈ Hᵖ(G, Hom_k(M', A)), y ∈ H^q(G, Hom_k(M, M')), z ∈ H_{p+q}(G, M), composition and evaluation as pairings; for x = 1, ⟨y, z⟩ is the image of y ∩ z in H₀(G, A) = A.

api.name: eval_eq_cap_IIT
api.statement: For k = A = ℂ_p, the evaluation Hⁿ(G, M^∨) ⊗ Hₙ(G, M) → ℂ_p is IntegralIwasawaTheoryPartII §0.7's cap product, under [g₁|…|gₙ] ↔ (1, g₁, …, g₁⋯gₙ).

tests.name: cap_Z2_perfect
tests.statement: G = ℤ/2, 𝔽₂: evaluation H¹ ⊗ H₁ → 𝔽₂ is perfect.

tests.name: cap_finite_index_zero
tests.statement: Degree 0: both sides of cor(x ∩ tr z) = cor(x) ∩ z are Σ_{gH} [μ(g·x ⊗ n)].

tests.name: eval_torus
tests.statement: Coordinate classes x, y of ℤ²: ⟨x ∪ y, [e₁|e₂] − [e₂|e₁]⟩ = 1 and ⟨y ∪ x, [e₁|e₂] − [e₂|e₁]⟩ = −1.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.cup_eq_tateCup
targets.statement: (a) For finite G, p, q ≥ 1, TateCohomology.isoGroupCohomology carries ∪ for 𝟙 to TauCeti.TateCohomology.cup, and degree 0 through H⁰ ↠ Ĥ⁰; (b) for discrete G, Θ (1.5) carries TauCeti.TopPairing.cup to ∪; (c) for profinite G, TauCeti.TopPairing.cup is the colimit of the cups on G ⧸ U.

tests.name: tate_Z2
tests.statement: G = ℤ/2: both send (x, x) to the nonzero class of H²(G, 𝔽₂).

tests.name: tate_norm_zero
tests.statement: Norm elements of Ĥ⁰ cup to zero in positive degree, as in H^q by the projection formula.

tests.name: profinite_abstract
tests.statement: G = ∏_ℕ ℤ/p: H¹_cont countable, abstract H¹ uncountable; only finite quotients are compared.

layers.title: Products of groups and abelian groups

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.cross
targets.statement: C(G; M) ⊗_k C(H; N) ≃ C(G × H; M ⊠ N) (homotopy equivalence); natural cross product H_p(G, M) ⊗ H_q(H, N) → H_{p+q}(G × H, M ⊠ N) induced by the Eilenberg–Zilber shuffle map ([g] × [h] = [(g,1)|(1,h)] − [(1,h)|(g,1)] for trivial coefficients); for k of global dimension ≤ 1 and N k-projective, the Künneth short exact sequence with Tor₁ terms, split when M is k-projective; over a field the cross product is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: for the sequence: k of global dimension ≤ 1, N projective over k

api.name: cross_natural
api.statement: Natural in compatible pairs on both factors, bilinear.

api.name: cross_assoc_comm
api.statement: Associative and graded commutative under G × H ≅ H × G with sign (−1)^{pq}.

tests.name: kunneth_V4_H3
tests.statement: H₃(ℤ/2 × ℤ/2, ℤ) = (ℤ/2)³: the cross product is not surjective.

tests.name: kunneth_Fp
tests.statement: Hₙ(ℤ/p × ℤ/p, 𝔽_p) = 𝔽_p^{n+1}.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.universalCoefficients
targets.statement: For k of global dimension ≤ 1 and trivial A: 0 → Hₙ(G, k) ⊗ A → Hₙ(G, A) → Tor₁(Hₙ₋₁(G, k), A) → 0 and 0 → Ext¹(Hₙ₋₁(G, k), A) → Hⁿ(G, A) → Hom(Hₙ(G, k), A) → 0, natural, split not naturally; the second map is the evaluation.
hypotheses: A a k-module with trivial action

tests.name: uct_Z2
tests.statement: H²(ℤ/2, 𝔽₂) = Ext¹(ℤ/2, 𝔽₂) = 𝔽₂.

tests.name: uct_field
tests.statement: Over a field Hⁿ(G, A) = Hom(Hₙ(G, k), A).

tests.name: uct_tor_needed
tests.statement: H₂(ℤ/2, ℤ/2) = ℤ/2 comes from the Tor term.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.cross
targets.statement: x × y = pr₁^*x ∪ pr₂^*y; for a field k, trivial coefficients and H_q(H, k) finite-dimensional for q ≤ n, ⊕_{p+q=n} Hᵖ(G, k) ⊗ H^q(H, k) → Hⁿ(G × H, k) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: dim H_q(H, k) < ∞ for q ≤ n

locator.where: Outlook 3.2.26, p. 138 (Loh19 line 5985–5994), statement without proof; the generality follows from 5.1 and 5.2

api.name: cross_natural_cohom
api.statement: Bilinear and natural in compatible pairs on both factors and in the coefficients.

api.name: cross_one
api.statement: x × 1 = pr₁^*x and 1 × y = pr₂^*y.

api.name: cross_comm
api.statement: τ^*(y × x) = (−1)^{pq} x × y under τ : G × H ≅ H × G.

api.name: cross_eval
api.statement: ⟨x × y, a × b⟩ = ⟨x, a⟩⟨y, b⟩ for trivial coefficients, with the evaluation of 4.6 and the shuffle cross product of 5.1.

api.name: cross_kunneth
api.statement: For a field k and H_q(H, k) finite-dimensional for q ≤ n, ⊕_{p+q=n} Hᵖ(G, k) ⊗ H^q(H, k) ≅ Hⁿ(G × H, k).

tests.name: cross_Fp
tests.statement: dim Hⁿ(ℤ/p × ℤ/p, 𝔽_p) = n + 1.

tests.name: cross_infinite
tests.statement: G = H = ℤ^(ℕ), k = ℚ: not surjective in degree 2.

tests.name: cross_trivial_factor
tests.statement: H trivial: the map is pr₁^*.

tests.name: cross_eval_11
tests.statement: G = H = ℤ, k = ℚ, identity characters x, y, a = b = [1]: a × b = [e₁|e₂] − [e₂|e₁], ⟨x × y, a × b⟩ = 1 − 0 = 1 = ⟨x, a⟩⟨y, b⟩; the Koszul sign (−1)^{|y||a|} gives −1.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.pontryagin
targets.statement: For abelian A, H•(A, k) is a graded-commutative associative unital k-algebra under the Pontryagin product, natural in A, with degree-one classes squaring to zero; ψ : Λ_k(A ⊗ k) → H•(A, k) is an isomorphism in degrees ≤ 2 for k = ℤ, in all degrees for torsion-free A and for ℚ-algebras k; over a field H•(A × B, k) ≅ H•(A, k) ⊗ H•(B, k) as algebras.

api.name: pontryagin_natural
api.statement: A homomorphism of abelian groups induces a homomorphism of graded k-algebras.

api.name: pontryagin_algebra
api.statement: Associative, unital (1 ∈ H₀(A, k) = k) and graded commutative.

api.name: pontryagin_degree_one
api.statement: H₁(A, k) ≅ A ⊗ k and x² = 0 there, so ψ : Λ_k(A ⊗ k) → H•(A, k) is defined.

api.name: pontryagin_integral
api.statement: For k = ℤ, ψ is an isomorphism in degrees ≤ 2; H₂(A, ℤ) ≅ Λ²A.

api.name: pontryagin_torsionFree
api.statement: For torsion-free A and every k, ψ is an isomorphism in all degrees.

api.name: pontryagin_rational
api.statement: For a ℚ-algebra k and every A, ψ is an isomorphism in all degrees.

api.name: pontryagin_product
api.statement: Over a field, H•(A × B, k) ≅ H•(A, k) ⊗ H•(B, k) as graded algebras.

tests.name: pont_Zn
tests.statement: H•(ℤⁿ, ℤ) ≅ Λ(ℤⁿ), ranks C(n, i), as AlgebraicTopology §5.4.

tests.name: pont_degree3
tests.statement: Λ³(ℤ/2) = 0 but H₃(ℤ/2, ℤ) = ℤ/2.

tests.name: pont_Q
tests.statement: ℚ = ⋃ (1/m!)ℤ: colim of H₁ = ℤ along ×(m+1) is ℚ = H₁(ℚ, ℤ), H₂(ℚ, ℤ) = Λ²ℚ = 0; class-surjectivity alone leaves H₁ a quotient of ℚ.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.extensionFiltration
targets.statement: Normalized cochains C̄(G, M) (a subcomplex, inclusion a quasi-isomorphism) and the filtration A_j: all of C̄ⁿ for j ≤ 0, cochains vanishing whenever n − j + 1 arguments lie in N for 0 < j ≤ n, zero for j > n; subcomplexes, finite, multiplicative, natural; A*_j gives the same spectral sequence from E₁.

locator.where: Ch. II §1, filtrations, Prop. 1 and Lemma 1, pp. 118–121 (HS53 line 368–411)

api.name: normalized_quasiIso
api.statement: C̄(G, M) ↪ C(G, M) is a quasi-isomorphism.

api.name: filtration_finite
api.statement: A_j ∩ C̄ⁿ = C̄ⁿ for j ≤ 0, A_{n+1} ∩ C̄ⁿ = 0, d(A_j) ⊂ A_j, A_{j+1} ⊂ A_j; as F_t = A_{−t}, F_t = C̄ for t ≥ 0. The filtration is bounded in each degree; a global lower bound is not guaranteed: some F_t is zero exactly when N = G or M = 0 (then F_{−1} = A_1 = 0), and for N ≠ G, M ≠ 0 the cochain of degree j ≥ 1 with value m ≠ 0 at (g, …, g), g ∉ N, and 0 elsewhere lies in A_j.

api.name: filtration_cup
api.statement: A_r ∪ B_s ⊂ C_{r+s} for a pairing.

api.name: filtration_natural
api.statement: A morphism of pairs (G', N') → (G, N) with a compatible coefficient map sends A_j into A_j.

api.name: filtration_star
api.statement: A*_j ⊂ A_j induces an isomorphism of spectral sequences from E₁.

tests.name: filt_N_trivial
tests.statement: N = 1: filtration by degree, E₂^{p,0} = Hᵖ(G, M); for G = ℤ/2, M = 𝔽₂, C̄ⁿ = 𝔽₂ ⊂ A_j for every n ≥ max(j, 0), so every F_t is nonzero.

tests.name: filt_N_G
tests.statement: N = G: A_j ∩ C̄ⁿ = 0 for j > 0, single column; for G = ℤ/2, M = 𝔽₂, C̄ⁿ = 𝔽₂ in every degree (C̄ unbounded) yet F_{−1} = A_1 = 0.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.hochschildSerre
targets.statement: Realises MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresentations §1.1's spectral sequence as that of F_t = A_{−t} (classical E_r^{p,q} at (2p + q + 1, −p − 1) on Mathlib page r + 1): E₁^{p,q} ≅ C̄^p(Q, H^q(N, M)) by restricting the first q arguments of A*_p-representatives to N, d₁ = (−1)^q times the coboundary, E₂^{p,q} ≅ Hᵖ(Q, H^q(N, M)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(G, M); E_∞^{p,q} ≅ A_pH^{p+q}/A_{p+1}H^{p+q}, the hypotheses of filtrationSpectralSequencePageXIsoEInfty holding from page max(q + 3, p + 2); natural for morphisms of extensions.

locator.where: Ch. II §2 Thm. 1, p. 121; Ch. II §4 Thm. 2, p. 125

tests.name: hs_extremes
tests.statement: N = 1: one row; N = G: one column.

tests.name: hs_S3
tests.statement: G = S₃, N = A₃, 𝔽₃: H^q(S₃, 𝔽₃) = 𝔽₃ for q ≡ 0, 3 mod 4, else 0.

tests.name: hs_Z4
tests.statement: ℤ/2 ⊂ ℤ/4, 𝔽₂: E₂ = 𝔽₂ everywhere but Hⁿ = 𝔽₂, so E₂ ≠ E_∞.

tests.name: hs_no_global_bound
tests.statement: N = 1, G = ℤ/2, 𝔽₂: every A_j is nonzero, so the finite-filtration theorem does not apply; in bidegree (p, 0) the vanishing hypotheses hold from page max(3, p + 2) and E_∞^{p,0} = 𝔽₂.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.hochschildSerre
targets.statement: For C_N(M) = (P ⊗ M)_N as a complex of Q-representations, Hₙ(Q; C_N(M)) ≅ Hₙ(G, M) and H_q(C_N(M)) ≅ H_q(N, M), giving E²_{p,q} = H_p(Q, H_q(N, M)) ⇒ H_{p+q}(G, M), natural.

tests.name: hsh_extremes
tests.statement: N = 1 and N = G: one row, one column.

tests.name: hsh_Z4
tests.statement: ℤ/2 ⊂ ℤ/4, 𝔽₂: E² = 𝔽₂ everywhere, Hₙ(ℤ/4, 𝔽₂) = 𝔽₂, so d² ≠ 0.

tests.name: hsh_V4
tests.statement: ℤ/2 × ℤ/2: degenerates, dim Hₙ = n + 1 as in 5.1.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.hochschildSerre_edge
targets.statement: Cohomological edge maps are inflation and restriction; homological edge maps are corestriction (inclusion-induced) and coinflation.

tests.name: edge_N_G
tests.statement: N = G: restriction edge is the identity.

tests.name: edge_N_trivial
tests.statement: N = 1: inflation edge is the identity.

tests.name: edge_Z4
tests.statement: ℤ/2 ⊂ ℤ/4, 𝔽₂: inflation on H¹ is an isomorphism, restriction on H¹ is zero.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.hochschildSerre_cup
targets.statement: For μ : M ⊗ M' ⟶ P, the pages carry pairings with d_r derivations (d_r(u ∪ v) = d_r u ∪ v + (−1)^{p+q} u ∪ d_r v); for u ∈ E₂^{p,q}, v ∈ E₂^{p',q'}, under the restriction identification of 6.2, u ∪ v is (−1)^{pq'} times the cup on Q with coefficients paired by the cup on N; on E_∞ it is induced by the cup on G with A_pH ∪ A_{p'}H ⊂ A_{p+p'}H.

locator.where: Ch. II §5 Thm. 3 and the remark after it, p. 126 (HS53 line 686–700)

tests.name: mult_N_trivial
tests.statement: N = 1: the cup product on G.

tests.name: mult_V4
tests.statement: ℤ/2 × ℤ/2 ⊃ 0 × ℤ/2, 𝔽₂: E₂ = 𝔽₂[x] ⊗ 𝔽₂[y].

tests.name: mult_sign
tests.statement: ℤ × ℤ ⊃ 0 × ℤ, M = ℤ, x ∈ E₂^{1,0}, y ∈ E₂^{0,1} identity characters: ỹ ∪ x̃ ∈ A*_1 restricts to (σ, γ) ↦ y(σ)x(γ), so y ∪ x ↦ +x·y and x ∪ y ↦ −x·y, as (−1)^{pq'} predicts; (−1)^{qp'} gives the opposite values, and anticommutativity alone does not distinguish them.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.transgression
targets.statement: x ∈ Hⁿ(N, M) is transgressive if some f ∈ C̄ⁿ(G, M) restricts to a representing cocycle and has df inflated from c ∈ C̄ⁿ⁺¹(Q, M^N); τ(x) = [c] in E_{n+1}^{n+1,0}. Transgressive classes are the image of E_{n+1}^{0,n} and τ = d_{n+1}; for n = 1, with MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresentations §1.1's section lift, every Q-invariant class is transgressive and τ = tg = d₂; if N acts trivially on M, d₂(u) = −c ∪ u with c the class of 1 → N^ab → G ⧸ [N, N] → Q → 1.
hypotheses: for d₂ = −c ∪: N acts trivially on M

locator.where: Ch. III §3 Prop. 1, pp. 128–129; Ch. III §6 Thm. 4, p. 133

api.name: transgressive_submodule
api.statement: The transgressive classes form a k-submodule of Hⁿ(N, M)^Q.

api.name: transgressive_iff
api.statement: Transgressive iff in the image of E_{n+1}^{0,n}; τ is well defined with values in E_{n+1}^{n+1,0}, k-linear, and τ = d_{n+1}.

api.name: transgression_one
api.statement: For n = 1, τ is defined on all of H¹(N, M)^Q for every group and equals MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresentations §1.1's tg and d₂.

api.name: transgression_natural
api.statement: τ commutes with maps induced by morphisms of extensions with compatible coefficient maps.

api.name: d2_eq_neg_cup
api.statement: d₂ = −c ∪ when N acts trivially.

tests.name: tg_Z4
tests.statement: ℤ/2 ⊂ ℤ/4, 𝔽₂: τ is the nonzero class.

tests.name: tg_sign_Z9
tests.statement: ℤ/3 ⊂ ℤ/9, 𝔽₃: τ(u) = −[carry]; d₂ = +c ∪ would give the other generator.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.fiveTerm_exact
targets.statement: For m ≥ 2 and H^q(N, M) = 0 for 0 < q < m: 0 → H^m(Q, M^N) → H^m(G, M) → H^m(N, M)^Q →τ H^{m+1}(Q, M^N) → H^{m+1}(G, M) exact, all of H^m(N, M)^Q transgressive (m = 1 is MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresentations §1.1's five-term sequence, with τ of 6.6); homological five-term sequence H₂(G, M) → H₂(Q, M_N) → H₁(N, M)_Q → H₁(G, M) → H₁(Q, M_N) → 0.
hypotheses: m ≥ 2 and H^q(N, M) = 0 for 0 < q < m

locator.where: Ch. III §4 Thm. 2 and the remark after it, pp. 129–130

tests.name: ft_extremes
tests.statement: N = 1 and N = G: isomorphisms of the outer terms.

tests.name: ft_degree_two
tests.statement: 2ℤ/4 ⊂ ℤ/4, M = ℤ, m = 2: 0 → ℤ/2 → ℤ/4 → ℤ/2 → H³(ℤ/2, ℤ) = 0; with M = 𝔽₂, H¹(N, 𝔽₂) ≠ 0 and inflation H²(ℤ/2, 𝔽₂) → H²(ℤ/4, 𝔽₂) is zero.

tests.name: ft_homological
tests.statement: ℤ/2 ⊂ ℤ/4, M = ℤ: 0 → H₁(N)_Q = ℤ/2 → ℤ/4 → ℤ/2 → 0, corestriction 1 ↦ 2.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupHomology.hopfFormula
targets.statement: For F = FreeGroup S, R ◁ F, G = F ⧸ R: H₂(G, ℤ) ≅ (R ⊓ ⁅F, F⁆) ⧸ ⁅F, R⁆, natural in presentations. The central-extension sequence is InductionRestrictionPartII RS.0.1's.

tests.name: hopf_cyclic
tests.statement: G = ℤ/n, F = ℤ, R = nℤ: H₂ = 0; the model R/[F, R] would give nℤ ≅ ℤ.

tests.name: hopf_Z2
tests.statement: G = ℤ²: R = [F, F], [F,F]/[F,[F,F]] ≅ ℤ, H₂ = ℤ.

tests.name: hopf_free
tests.statement: G = F free, R = 1: both sides 0, as 3.6 requires.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.fiveTerm_eq_continuous
targets.statement: For finite discrete G, the cohomological five-term sequence (MappingClassGroupsAndCanonicalRepresentations §1.1, with τ of 6.6) corresponds under Θ and ProfiniteCohomology §3.1 to ProfiniteCohomology §5.5, and τ is TauCeti.ContCohomology.transgression; the comparison is fixed by the pinned definitions, HS53 supplying only the sequence.

locator.where: Ch. III §4, remark after Thm. 2, p. 130 (HS53 line 854–856), for the five-term sequence only

tests.name: cmp_Z9
tests.statement: ℤ/3 ⊂ ℤ/9: both give −[carry].

tests.name: cmp_N_G
tests.statement: N = G: both transgressions land in H²(1, −) = 0.

tests.name: cmp_section
tests.statement: For finite G every section is continuous, so the lifts coincide.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.res_comp_corestriction_eq_sum
targets.statement: For any G, H ≤ G of finite index, K ≤ G: res^G_K ∘ cor^G_H = Σ_{KgH} cor^K_{K∩gHg⁻¹} ∘ c_g ∘ res^H_{H∩g⁻¹Kg}, summands independent of g; homologically tr^G_H ∘ cor^G_K = Σ_{KgH} cor^H_{H∩g⁻¹Kg} ∘ c_{g⁻¹} ∘ tr^K_{K∩gHg⁻¹}.

tests.name: mackey_continuous
tests.statement: For finite G agrees under Θ with TauCeti.ContinuousCohomology.corestriction_mackey; S₃, H = K = ⟨(12)⟩: res ∘ cor = id in positive degrees.

tests.name: mackey_K_trivial
tests.statement: K = 1, degree 0: Σ_{gH} g·m.

tests.name: mackey_normal
tests.statement: K = H normal: res cor = Σ_{gH} c_g.

tests.name: mackey_homology_reps
tests.statement: c_g instead of c_{g⁻¹} lands outside H.

targets.name: TauCeti.groupCohomology.stableElements
targets.statement: For finite G, a Sylow p-subgroup P and n ≥ 1, restriction maps Hⁿ(G, M)(p) isomorphically onto the stable classes; homological corestriction maps the transfer-stable classes of Hₙ(P, M) onto Hₙ(G, M)(p); in Tate cohomology for all n ∈ ℤ; for abelian P and trivial action of G on M the stable classes are the N_G(P)-invariants. For M = ℤ_(r) it is K3BlochGroups §5.2's stable-element theorem.
hypotheses: abelian simplification: P abelian and G acting trivially on M

api.name: stable_submodule
api.statement: Stable classes form a k-submodule containing the restriction (transfer) of every class of G.

api.name: stable_cohomology
api.statement: n ≥ 1: res^G_P : Hⁿ(G, M)(p) ≅ stable classes, inverse [G : P]⁻¹ cor.

api.name: stable_homology
api.statement: n ≥ 1: homological corestriction from the stable classes of Hₙ(P, M) onto Hₙ(G, M)(p) is an isomorphism.

api.name: stable_tate
api.statement: Every n ∈ ℤ: res^G_P : Ĥⁿ(G, M)(p) ≅ stable classes of Ĥⁿ(P, M).

api.name: stable_abelian
api.statement: P abelian, trivial action: stable classes = N_G(P)-invariants.

api.name: stable_K3_comparison
api.statement: M = ℤ_(r), p = r, n ≥ 1: the cohomological isomorphism is K3BlochGroups §5.2's.

tests.name: stable_p_group
tests.statement: G = P: every class is stable.

tests.name: stable_degree_zero
tests.statement: n = 0, M = ℤ: H⁰(G, ℤ)(p) = 0 but all of H⁰(P, ℤ) = ℤ is stable.

tests.name: stable_twisted
tests.statement: G = C₂ × S₃, p = 2, P = C₂ × ⟨(12)⟩ = N_G(P), M = 𝔽₂³ permutation module: the cocycle z ↦ e₃, (12) ↦ 0 is N_G(P)-invariant but c_{(23)} sends its restriction to ⟨z⟩ to e₂ ≠ e₃; invariants have dimension 3, stable classes dimension 2.

layers.title: Tate duality and periodicity of finite groups

targets.name: TauCeti.TateCohomology.tateDuality
targets.statement: Cup with evaluation M^∨ ⊗ M → ℚ/ℤ and Ĥ⁻¹(G, ℚ/ℤ) ⊂ ℚ/ℤ gives Ĥⁱ(G, M^∨) ≅ Hom(Ĥ^{−1−i}(G, M), ℚ/ℤ) for all i; for ℤ-free M, Ĥⁱ(G, Hom(M, ℤ)) ≅ Hom(Ĥ^{−i}(G, M), ℚ/ℤ). For M = ℤ and i ≥ 1 this is K3BlochGroups §5.2's H^{i+1}(G, ℤ) ≅ Hom(H_i(G, ℤ), ℚ/ℤ).
hypotheses: integral form: M free as an abelian group

tests.name: tate_dual_Z2
tests.statement: G = ℤ/2, M = ℤ: Ĥ⁰(ℚ/ℤ) = 0, Ĥ¹(ℚ/ℤ) = ℤ/2 = Hom(H₁, ℚ/ℤ).

tests.name: tate_dual_d0
tests.statement: Integral instance needs i ≥ 1: H²(ℤ/2, ℤ) = ℤ/2 = Hom(H₁, ℚ/ℤ), but in degree 0, H¹(G, ℤ) = 0 while Hom(H₀, ℚ/ℤ) = ℚ/ℤ.

tests.name: tate_dual_free
tests.statement: M = ℤ/2 not free: Ĥ⁰(Hom(M, ℤ)) = 0 but the dual of Ĥ⁰(ℤ/2, ℤ/2) is ℤ/2.

targets.name: TauCeti.IsPGroup.isCyclic_or_quaternion
targets.statement: A finite p-group whose abelian subgroups are cyclic is cyclic (p odd), or cyclic or ≅ QuaternionGroup (2^(s−2)), s ≥ 3 (p = 2); conversely cyclic and generalised quaternion groups have all abelian subgroups cyclic.

tests.name: burnside_Q8
tests.statement: Q₈: abelian subgroups ⟨i⟩, ⟨j⟩, ⟨k⟩, ⟨−1⟩, 1 cyclic.

tests.name: burnside_D8
tests.statement: D₈ and ℤ/p × ℤ/p contain ℤ/p × ℤ/p.

tests.name: burnside_heisenberg
tests.statement: p odd: the Heisenberg group of order p³ contains ℤ/p × ℤ/p.

targets.name: TauCeti.TateCohomology.periodic_of_exact
targets.statement: An exact sequence 0 → ℤ_χ → C_n → … → C_0 → ℤ → 0 with each C_i ℤ-free and cohomologically trivial gives, by cup with the iterated connecting class e ∈ Ĥⁿ⁺¹(G, ℤ_χ), isomorphisms Ĥⁱ(G, M) ≅ Ĥ^{i+n+1}(G, M ⊗ ℤ_χ); period divides 2(n+1), and n+1 if χ is trivial; such a sequence exists for a bounded complex of free ℤ[G]-modules with homology ℤ in degree 0 and ℤ_χ in degree n ≥ 1.
hypotheses: C_i free abelian and cohomologically trivial

locator.where: Thm. 4.3.7, p. 165, and its proof, pp. 165–167

tests.name: free_cyclic_circle
tests.statement: ℤ/m with 0 → ℤ → ℤG → ℤG → ℤ → 0: period divides 2.

tests.name: free_n_zero
tests.statement: ℤ/2, n = 0: 0 → ℤ_sgn → ℤG → ℤ → 0, period divides 2.

tests.name: free_CpCp
tests.statement: C_p × C_p admits no such sequence.

targets.name: TauCeti.TateCohomology.pPeriod
targets.statement: p-period = least d > 0 with Ĥ^d(G, ℤ)(p) cyclic of order |G|_p (p ∣ |G|). Cyclic G: cup with δχ ∈ Ĥ²(G, ℤ) is periodicity in all degrees; Q_{2^s}: K3BlochGroups §5.2's four-periodic resolution and 8.3 give periodicity with u ∈ Ĥ⁴ for every M, 2-period 4. Swan's theorem (odd p, cyclic Sylow P: 2|N_G(P)/C_G(P)|; 2-period 2 or 4) is K3BlochGroups §5.2's, for this period.

locator.where: Ch. XII (generalised quaternion periodicity; uncertified); Swan's theorem SwanPPeriod60 Thms. 1 and 2 (waived; Hutchinson13 Thm. 3.1, p. 12) through K3BlochGroups §5.2

api.name: pPeriod_def
api.statement: The least d > 0 with Ĥ^d(G, ℤ)(p) cyclic of order |G|_p, for p ∣ |G| when such d exists.

api.name: pPeriod_ge_two
api.statement: The p-period is at least 2, since Ĥ¹(G, ℤ) = 0 and |G|_p > 1.

api.name: pPeriod_cyclic
api.statement: G cyclic of order m, p ∣ m: p-period 2.

api.name: pPeriod_quaternion
api.statement: Q_{2^s}, s ≥ 3: 2-period 4.

api.name: pPeriod_eq_K3
api.statement: For d ≥ 2, Ĥ^d(G, ℤ)(p) is cyclic of order |G|_p iff H_{d−1}(G, ℤ_(p)) is (8.1), so the p-period is K3BlochGroups §5.2's.

tests.name: swan_S3
tests.statement: S₃: 3-period 4, 2-period 2.

tests.name: swan_SL2
tests.statement: SL₂(𝔽_q), q odd: 2-period 4, H_k(−, ℤ_(2)) = ℤ_(2)/q(q²−1) for k ≡ 3 mod 4.

tests.name: swan_coprime
tests.statement: p ∤ |G|: the least d is 1, not 2|N/C| = 2.

targets.name: TauCeti.TateCohomology.periodic_tfae
targets.statement: TFAE for finite G: (a) cup with some u ∈ Ĥ^d(G, ℤ), d > 0, is an isomorphism in all degrees for all M; (b) Ĥ^d(G, ℤ) cyclic of order |G| for some d ≠ 0; (c) every abelian subgroup cyclic; (d) every Sylow subgroup cyclic or generalised quaternion; and the p-primary form.

tests.name: per_CpCp
tests.statement: C_p × C_p: dim Hⁿ(−, 𝔽_p) = n + 1 unbounded, not periodic.

tests.name: per_SL2
tests.statement: SL₂(𝔽_q), q = p^f odd: Sylow 2 generalised quaternion, Sylow ℓ cyclic for odd ℓ ≠ p, 2-period 4; the Sylow p-subgroup (𝔽_q, +) ≅ (ℤ/p)^f is cyclic iff f = 1. SL₂(𝔽₉) is not periodic: its unipotent ℤ/3 × ℤ/3 is a full Sylow 3-subgroup (|SL₂(𝔽₉)| = 720).

tests.name: per_trivial
tests.statement: Trivial group: all conditions hold with u = 0; S₃ has d = 4; A₄ fails (c).

suppliers.what: First-quadrant double-complex spectral sequences (cohomological and homological): E₂, convergence, edge morphisms, five-term and extended sequences, exact-rows comparison, naturality.
Explicit low-degree comparisons, profinite five-term sequence, continuous Mackey formula, finite-quotient colimit, continuous cup product; used in the comparisons 1.5, 4.7, 6.9 and a Check of 7.1.
Tate-cohomology interface: restriction, corestriction, cohomological triviality, Nakayama–Rim.
G-trees, Bass–Serre trees, one-edge splittings as PushoutI and HNNExtension, free groups as fundamental groups of roses.
Cartan–Leray for finite regular covers, torus homology and C_p × C_p actions, for Checks.

Integral group hyperhomology of complexes in degrees ≥ 0 with its two spectral sequences, vanishing and permutation-module Shapiro identification (compared with 2.1, 2.3, 3.2); the directed-union identification H_m(G, A) = colim H_m(G_i, A) for any coefficient ring (used in 5.4).

Bounded-below reindexing of integral hyperhomology (compared with 2.1); for finite groups the stable-element theorem with ℤ_(r) coefficients (compared with 7.2), the duality H^{d+1}(G, ℤ) ≅ Hom(H_d(G, ℤ), ℚ/ℤ) (compared with 8.1), the four-periodic resolution of Q_{2^s} and Swan's r-period theorem (used in 8.4, 8.5).

Existence and naturality of the cohomological Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence of a discrete extension, the section lift and transgression in degree one, and the cohomological five-term exact sequence (realised in 6.2, used in 6.6, 6.7, 6.9).
The cap product H^q(U, M^∨) × H_q(U, M) → ℂ_p, compared with the evaluation pairing of 4.6.

gaps.title: Homological edge morphisms and five-term sequence of a first-quadrant double complex
gaps.detail: DerivedModuleAlgebra §S.1 states edge morphisms and the five-term and extended sequences in cohomological indexing; its homological form gives E² and convergence only.
gaps.needs: The edge morphisms H_n(Tot C) → E²_{n,0}, E²_{0,n} → H_n(Tot C) and the exact sequence H₂(Tot C) → E²_{2,0} → E²_{0,1} → H₁(Tot C) → E²_{1,0} → 0 for a first-quadrant homological double complex.
